purpose: Eighteenth expanded public source layer focused on whole-route and source-governance boundaries beyond ordinary reaction templates: route economics and PMI, scalable purification/isolation bottlenecks, formulation and solid-form developability, photostability/autoxidation storage liability, biosynthetic-origin and isotope/biogenic annotation, bioassay and binding-mode source validation, genotoxic/nitrosamine impurity precursor liability, and controlled, stewardship-sensitive, dual-use, or regulated route governance.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, process, analytical, toxicology, formulation, biosynthesis, biology, regulatory, safety, and governance review

explicit whole-route economics, separation evidence, developability data, stability-indicating evidence, biosynthetic lineage, target-validation evidence, impurity-risk assessment, or governance authorization before proposal promotion

separate process-economics, purification, formulation, stability, biosynthetic-origin, assay-validation, genotoxic-impurity, controlled-substance, stewardship, dual-use, cytotoxic, radiochemical, and environmental-persistence policy

route-specific PMI or step-economy evidence, impurity purge and scalable isolation evidence, salt/coformer or delivery characterization, forced-degradation or photostability data, isotope/genome/metabolome support, potency/selectivity/target-engagement and assay-interference controls, nitrosamine or mutagenic-impurity risk assessment, and project governance review
safety, toxicology, antimicrobial-stewardship, controlled-substance, dual-use, environmental, regulatory, analytical-validation, formulation, and biological-mode review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operating conditions, hazardous execution instructions, purification recipes, assay protocols, biological handling steps, and scale-up instructions

v19 records are source-quality and route-choice priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated scalable processes, formulation endpoints, stable reference standards, validated biosynthetic origins, proven probes, impurity-safe routes, or authorized regulated work

families.name: Whole-route economics, process mass intensity, step count, convergence, yield, solvent burden, and manufacturing-cost policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a formally short route from whole-route resource intensity. Strategic value depends on step count, convergence, yield, solvent/workup burden, PMI, waste, and comparator process evidence rather than single-step template feasibility.

families.name: Scalable purification, isolation, crystallization, chromatography, extraction, distillation, and impurity-purge bottleneck policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate bond formation from the isolation operation that makes a route scalable. Purification, crystallization, washing, drying, extraction, distillation, chromatography, and impurity-purge records can dominate feasibility.

families.name: Formulation, salt, cocrystal, coformer, polymorph, particle-size, excipient, and delivery-boundary policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate synthetic endpoint from developable drug substance or product form. Salt, cocrystal, polymorph, hydrate, amorphous, particle-size, excipient, and delivery choices can define whether a route endpoint is meaningful.

families.name: Photostability, autoxidation, peroxide, radical, oxygen/moisture, and storage-liability policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate isolated compound access from evidence that the compound remains chemically assigned and usable under storage, light, oxygen, moisture, or formulation stress. Stability liabilities can invalidate source trust.

families.name: Biosynthetic origin, isotope tracing, biogenic precursor, pathway annotation, genome/metabolome, and source-lineage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a natural-product source claim from pathway evidence. Biosynthetic-origin records need isotope, genome, metabolome, enzyme, organism, and isolation-lineage support before they guide route critique or biomimetic proposals.

families.name: Bioassay, binding mode, selectivity, target engagement, chemical-probe, and assay-provenance source policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a bioactive structure from evidence that it is a trustworthy biological source. Probe and hit records require potency, selectivity, target engagement, assay lineage, interference controls, comparator analogues, and biological-mode context.

families.name: Genotoxic impurity, nitrosamine, azide, hydrazine, alkylating precursor, purge, and regulatory-liability policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate route feasibility from impurity liability. Mutagenic, nitrosamine, alkylating, azide, hydrazine, epoxide, and reactive precursor records need root-cause, purge, analytical, toxicology, and regulatory-control evidence.

families.name: Controlled, stewardship-sensitive, dual-use, radiochemical, cytotoxic, antimicrobial, persistent, and governed route-boundary policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate chemically possible routes from authorized, appropriate, and governed use. Controlled, stewardship-sensitive, dual-use, cytotoxic, radiochemical, antimicrobial, endocrine-active, or persistent records must carry explicit governance metadata.

anchors.name: Whole-route economics anchor with reviewed PMI, step count, convergence, solvent/workup burden, yield, and comparator-process evidence
Isolation bottleneck anchor with reviewed crystallization, chromatography, washing, drying, phase behavior, and impurity-purge evidence
aliases: filter cake wash and isolation record

anchors.name: Formulation/solid-form anchor with reviewed salt or coformer choice, polymorph/hydrate identity, particle attributes, excipient compatibility, and delivery evidence
Stability-liability anchor with reviewed photostability, oxidative degradation, peroxide/radical risk, storage state, degradant identity, and stability-indicating assay
Biosynthetic-origin anchor with reviewed isotope tracing, biogenic precursor, biosynthetic gene cluster, organism, metabolome, and pathway-lineage evidence
Biological-source anchor with reviewed potency, selectivity, binding mode, target engagement, assay lineage, interference controls, and comparator analogues
Genotoxic/nitrosamine impurity anchor with reviewed precursor root cause, purge path, analytical method, toxicology limit, and regulatory-control evidence
Governed-route anchor with reviewed controlled-substance, stewardship, dual-use, cytotoxic, radiochemical, persistence, authorization, access, and use-case metadata

disconnections.name: Target route to convergent branch map plus PMI, step count, solvent/workup burden, and comparator-process boundary

break_bonds: target route to whole-route PMI boundary
linear route to convergent-branch comparator boundary
forward_logic: separate a formally valid bond-disconnection sequence from the mass and waste required across the whole route
track longest linear sequence, convergence, isolated yields, solvent and workup mass, and comparator process
avoid rewarding routes that look short but shift burden into purification, protection, or low-yield branches
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward route sources only when step count, convergence, PMI, yield, and solvent/workup burden are explicit.

evidence.citation: ACS GCI Pharmaceutical Roundtable describes PMI as a route-level metric that includes materials such as reactants, solvents, catalysts, and workup inputs.
Process Mass Intensity paper explains why PMI was selected as a high-level pharmaceutical manufacturing sustainability metric.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit whole-route mass ledger, convergence, isolated yields, solvent/workup burden, and comparator process

disconnections.name: Route endpoint to manufacturing-cost, solvent-class, raw-material, and sustainability-intensity policy

break_bonds: synthetic endpoint to manufacturing-cost boundary
laboratory solvent choice to process-intensity boundary
forward_logic: separate laboratory success from manufacturing cost, solvent burden, and sustainability intensity
track raw material price/grade, solvent-selection class, energy or cleaning burden, and process-change comparator
flag routes where low step count is offset by high material, solvent, or containment cost
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use route-intensity records when manufacturing economics or sustainability, not a single reaction, is route-defining.

evidence.citation: Manufacturing Mass Intensity article reviews 15 years of PMI use and extension to broader API manufacturing inputs.
ACS sustainability perspective discusses environmental sustainability strategy for API manufacturing and PMI/LCA concepts.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit cost, raw-material grade, solvent class, sustainability boundary, and process comparator

disconnections.name: Crude product to crystallization/isolation plus impurity incorporation, mother-liquor, wash, and purge-policy boundary

break_bonds: crude product to crystallization-purge boundary
isolated solid to mother-liquor and wash boundary
forward_logic: separate chemical conversion from the crystallization and isolation operation that determines purity
track impurity incorporation mechanism, phase behavior, mother-liquor fate, washing, drying, and analytical release method
avoid treating crystallization as generic cleanup when impurity purge is route-defining
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward crystallization-source routes only when impurity incorporation, wash, mother-liquor, and assay evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: Industrial crystallization workflow paper describes mechanisms of impurity incorporation and targeted impurity management.
API washing study discusses filtration, washing, mother liquor, and effects on final API purity.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit impurity purge, crystallization mechanism, mother-liquor fate, wash/dry evidence, and analytical assay

disconnections.name: Purified product to chromatography, membrane, extraction, distillation, or alternative scalable-isolation boundary

break_bonds: purified target to separation-scale boundary
chromatographic cleanup to isolation-feasibility boundary
forward_logic: separate product formation from the separation technology that controls scale, recovery, and waste
track chromatographic load, solvent use, stationary phase or membrane burden, extraction selectivity, distillation feasibility, and impurity profile
down-rank routes that depend on unbounded chromatography when scalable alternatives are missing
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use scalable-isolation records when separation technology, recovery, and solvent or material burden drive route feasibility.

evidence.citation: ACS GCI med-chem purification resources include green chromatography and purification decision guidance.
Preparative and analytical chromatography greenness review discusses solvent and productivity burdens in chromatographic methods.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit separation mode, load/recovery, solvent/material burden, impurity selectivity, and scale boundary

disconnections.name: Synthetic endpoint to salt, cocrystal, coformer, polymorph, hydrate, or amorphous developability boundary

break_bonds: free form to salt/coformer boundary
synthetic target to solid-form performance boundary
forward_logic: separate access to a molecular structure from evidence that its solid form is developable
track salt or coformer rationale, polymorph/hydrate identity, solubility/dissolution, stability, manufacturability, and regulatory classification
avoid treating a free base or acid endpoint as equivalent to a qualified product form
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward synthetic endpoints only when the salt, cocrystal, or polymorph identity and developability boundary are explicit.

evidence.citation: FDA cocrystal guidance discusses regulatory classification and data to support pharmaceutical cocrystal solid forms.
FDA ICH Q6A guidance discusses polymorphism and specifications for new drug substances and products.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit solid-form identity, salt/coformer rationale, solubility or performance data, stability, manufacturability, and regulatory classification

disconnections.name: Active compound to particle-size, excipient compatibility, delivery vehicle, and formulation-performance policy

break_bonds: isolated active to formulation-performance boundary
particle or excipient choice to delivery boundary
forward_logic: separate chemical identity from formulation attributes that control exposure and manufacturability
track particle size, excipient compatibility, dissolution, physical stability, delivery vehicle, and bioavailability context
flag routes where the synthetic endpoint is not the practical delivery endpoint
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use formulation records when delivery, particle attributes, or excipient compatibility determine whether the route endpoint is useful.

evidence.citation: Pharmaceutical cocrystal review discusses solid-form approaches to modulate solubility, dissolution, pharmacokinetics, and stability.
Pharmaceutical cocrystal regulatory and strategic review covers cocrystal development, physicochemical properties, and regulatory aspects.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit particle/excipient attributes, dissolution or exposure context, compatibility, and stability evidence

disconnections.name: Source compound to photostability and forced-degradation evidence plus stability-indicating method boundary

break_bonds: isolated compound to photostability boundary
degradant assignment to stability-indicating method boundary
forward_logic: separate source isolation from evidence that light or stress exposure does not change target identity
track photostability study, forced-degradation conditions, degradant identity, assay specificity, and storage recommendation
avoid promoting unstable source records without a stability-indicating method
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward stability-sensitive sources only when photostability, forced-degradation, and stability-indicating method evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: EMA ICH Q1B guidance covers photostability testing expectations for new active substances and medicinal products.
Forced-degradation review discusses development of stability-indicating studies and methods for drugs.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit photostability, forced degradation, degradant identity, method specificity, and storage policy

disconnections.name: Oxidation-sensitive target to oxygen, peroxide, radical, moisture, and storage-liability policy

break_bonds: isolated target to oxidative-liability boundary
storage source to oxygen/moisture exposure boundary
forward_logic: separate synthetic access from stability under oxygen, peroxide, radical, or moisture stress
track vulnerable functional groups, oxidative degradants, excipient or solvent peroxide sources, packaging/storage state, and retest policy
flag sources whose reference identity may drift during storage or handling
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use autoxidation records when storage liability or degradation, not synthesis, determines source trust.

evidence.citation: FDA ICH Q1A(R2) guidance describes stability testing of new drug substances and products.
Forced-degradation review discusses oxidative stress and peroxide-mediated degradation as method-development challenges.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit oxidative liability, degradant profile, storage state, packaging or retest policy, and analytical method

disconnections.name: Natural product to isotope-labeled precursor incorporation plus biosynthetic-origin evidence boundary

break_bonds: natural product skeleton to labeled-precursor boundary
biogenic claim to isotope-incorporation evidence boundary
forward_logic: separate a plausible biogenic disconnection from isotope evidence that supports the precursor lineage
track labeled precursor, incorporation pattern, analytical method, organism/source, and alternative pathway hypotheses
avoid promoting biomimetic route logic from unsupported biosynthetic stories
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward biosynthesis-aware route priors only when isotope incorporation and source lineage are explicit.

evidence.citation: Isotopic labeling approach links natural products with biosynthetic gene clusters and discusses stable-isotope patterns.
Stable isotope biosynthesis review emphasizes isotope labeling as an important natural-product pathway tool.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit labeled precursor, incorporation pattern, organism/source, analytical method, and pathway alternatives

disconnections.name: Natural product source to biosynthetic gene cluster, organism, metabolome, and structure-assignment policy

break_bonds: natural product source claim to BGC evidence boundary
metabolite annotation to structure-assignment boundary
forward_logic: separate metabolite detection from experimentally supported biosynthetic lineage
track BGC prediction, organism strain, expression context, metabolomic match, isolation evidence, and structure assignment
down-rank source records based only on genome prediction or MS similarity without chemical validation
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use BGC/metabolome records as advisory priors unless organism, pathway, metabolite, and structure evidence align.

evidence.citation: Meta-omic natural-product review discusses characterizing biosynthetic gene clusters and pathways.
Natural-products genomics/metabolomics review surveys integrated strategies for targeting new chemical entities.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit organism, BGC, expression/metabolome evidence, isolation, and structure assignment

disconnections.name: Bioactive compound to chemical-probe target engagement, selectivity, binding mode, and comparator-policy boundary

break_bonds: bioactive structure to target-engagement boundary
probe claim to selectivity and comparator boundary
forward_logic: separate a compound with activity from a probe-quality source record
track biochemical potency, cellular activity, target engagement, selectivity panel, binding-mode evidence, inactive analogue, and orthogonal validation
avoid promoting a route source because a structure is bioactive without target-validation support
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward bioactive source records only when target engagement, selectivity, binding mode, and comparator evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: High-quality chemical-probes review discusses potency, selectivity, target engagement, and inactive analogues.
Target-engagement review argues that engagement assays should be standard for chemical probe and drug-discovery programs.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit potency, selectivity, target engagement, binding mode, inactive analogue, and orthogonal validation

disconnections.name: Screening hit to assay-interference, PAINS/reactivity, aggregation, purity, and hit-lineage policy

break_bonds: screening activity to assay-interference boundary
hit structure to purity and validation lineage boundary
forward_logic: separate apparent assay activity from a validated biological source
track assay format, counter-screens, aggregation/reactivity, purity and stability in assay buffer, SAR consistency, and resynthesis
down-rank source records where assay interference or promiscuity has not been addressed
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use screening-hit records cautiously unless assay interference, purity, SAR, and validation lineage are explicit.

evidence.citation: Assay-interference review discusses PAINS, promiscuity, counter-screening, purity, and stability in assay buffers.
NCBI Assay Guidance Manual chapter covers chemical reactivity interference in target-based and cell-based assays.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit counter-screens, interference controls, purity, stability, SAR consistency, and resynthesis

disconnections.name: API route to nitrosamine or NDSRI precursor, root-cause, risk assessment, confirmatory testing, and control-policy boundary

break_bonds: API route to nitrosamine-root-cause boundary
amine/nitrite precursor pair to control-strategy boundary
forward_logic: separate route feasibility from nitrosamine formation risk and regulatory control
track amine and nitrosating sources, excipient or solvent contributions, process/storage conditions, analytical method, acceptable intake, and mitigation
avoid treating routes as clean unless nitrosamine root cause and control strategy are reviewed
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank nitrosation-risk routes unless root cause, confirmatory testing, mitigation, and regulatory limits are explicit.

evidence.citation: FDA nitrosamine guidance discusses root causes, detection, risk assessments, testing, and controls for APIs and drug products.
Nitrosamine systematic review covers toxicological implications, root causes, risk assessment, and mitigation strategies.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit nitrosating source, root-cause analysis, confirmatory method, acceptable intake, purge/mitigation, and regulatory control

disconnections.name: Synthetic route to mutagenic impurity precursor plus purge, analytical, toxicology, and regulatory-control policy

break_bonds: route precursor to mutagenic-impurity liability boundary
reactive impurity to purge and analytical-control boundary
forward_logic: separate useful reactive chemistry from genotoxic impurity liability
track structural alert, impurity formation pathway, purge factor, analytical method, toxicology threshold, and lifecycle control
flag routes where reactive precursors improve synthesis but create unbounded impurity risk
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use mutagenic-impurity records as hard route-quality constraints unless purge, method, toxicology, and control evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: ICH M7(R2) guidance covers assessment and control of DNA-reactive mutagenic impurities in pharmaceuticals.
Nitrosation pathway review notes risk evaluation for reactive genotoxic impurities such as azido, nitroso, epoxide, and hydrazine classes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit structural alert, formation route, purge factor, validated method, toxicology limit, and lifecycle controls

disconnections.name: Route target or precursor to controlled-substance/listed-chemical status, authorization, storage, recordkeeping, and access-policy boundary

break_bonds: regulated compound to authorization boundary
precursor source to controlled-access boundary
forward_logic: separate chemical route availability from legal authorization and secure handling
track schedule/list status, registration or exemption basis, storage and access controls, recordkeeping, disposal, and approved use case
do not promote controlled or listed source records without project-level governance approval
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat controlled or listed-chemical source records as governance-gated, not ordinary route anchors.

evidence.citation: DEA Chemical Handler's Manual summarizes basic requirements for handling List I and List II chemicals under the Controlled Substances Act.
University controlled-substance research guidance summarizes registration, storage, security, use, disposal, and records expectations.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: none without explicit legal authorization, access control, recordkeeping, and approved research or analytical use case

disconnections.name: Bioactive or regulated route to antimicrobial stewardship, dual-use, cytotoxic, radiochemical, persistence, and project-governance policy

break_bonds: bioactive route source to stewardship boundary
regulated capability to project-governance boundary
forward_logic: separate bioactive route plausibility from whether the work is appropriate, authorized, and governed
track stewardship rationale, use-case necessity, exposure or dissemination risk, access controls, review board or project approval, and release restrictions
avoid turning sensitive source records into proposal generators without governance metadata
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use stewardship and dual-use records only as policy gates unless explicit governance and use-case evidence exists.

evidence.citation: CDC core elements describe antibiotic stewardship principles to improve antibiotic use, patient safety, and resistance control.
NIH notice describes the 2024 US Government policy for oversight of dual-use research of concern and enhanced pandemic potential.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: none without explicit stewardship rationale, governance approval, access control, and approved use-case boundary

source_notes.summary: The v19 expansion promotes backlog families covering whole-route economics/PMI, purification and isolation bottlenecks, formulation and solid-form developability, stability liability, biosynthetic-origin evidence, biological-source validation, genotoxic/nitrosamine impurity liability, and governed regulated-source boundaries.

V19 records are advisory. Promotion requires route-specific evidence and governance; process, purification, formulation, stability, bioassay, impurity, controlled-substance, stewardship, and dual-use records must not be treated as executable procedures or validated route closures by default.
